gen-fs-trench-slab-gf-lexend-zetta: Lexend Zetta reads wide and tall-bodied, its ribbon-like strokes spaced far apart. Trench Slab is the serif up top, with oversized lowercase that gives the pair its industrial bite.
gen-fs-trench-slab-gf-montserrat-alterna: Trench Slab brings an industrial, oversized lowercase to the top of the page, built like a modern machine part. And Montserrat Alternates follows with wire-like sans-serif strokes and wide-open round letters that would keep a long read moving.
gen-fs-zina-author: Zina draws fat downstrokes against threadlike upstrokes, striking and refined in the way a broad-nib pen is. Author, a text serif, is the one better suited to brief copy.
gen-fs-zina-crimson-pro: Refined and striking, Zina sets closed, widely spaced letters with a hairline gap running through them. Crimson Pro answers with open shapes and a gentle thick-thin rhythm.
gen-fs-zina-gf-hepta-slab: Hepta Slab reads bookish and open, its round bowls holding the same wall all the way around. Over many paragraphs, Hepta Slab stretches each word out and lets the white space do the breathing, while Zina's closed heading letters stay sharply apart.
gen-fs-zina-gf-kiwi-maru: Hairline cracks meet a finger-trace outline here, with Zina's high-contrast letters sitting above Kiwi Maru's constant-width strokes. The strongest quality is that opposition: closed and spiky above, open and generous below.
gen-fs-zina-gf-padyakke-expanded-one: Zina leads with fat downstrokes and threadlike upstrokes. Padyakke Expanded One is a serif with pitcher-mouthed c shapes and glyphs spread wide, so if the heading shrinks or the body grows, that spacious sprawl would swallow the delicate hairlines.
gen-fs-zina-gf-stint-ultra-expanded: Sharp hairlines meet drifting, pipe-cleaner letters. Zina is best at striking, high-contrast display work, while Stint Ultra Expanded does its best work as a traditional, authoritative serif with open counters.
gen-gf-aboreto-archivo: Wide-spaced, ladle-bowled capitals sit up top, then Archivo takes over with outward-opening curves. Aboreto is best at expressive, commanding display moments, but Archivo is best at approachable editorial text.
gen-gf-aboreto-fs-asap: Heavy bowls with razor-fine tops define Aboreto, a display face with wide gaps between its letters. Asap, a sans-serif, does the readable work, with open arcs and a body height close to its capitals.
